hints.content:
To find the average rate of change $(ARC)$ of the function $f$ over the interval $[-3,9]$, we need to take the total change in the function value over the interval (which is the difference of its values at the endpoints) and divide it by the length of the interval:

 $ARC_{[-3,9]}= \dfrac{f(9)-f(-3)}{9-(-3)}$.

Note that this is the same as finding the slope of the line connecting the points on the graph that correspond to the endpoints of the interval:



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes each scale by one. The graph is a curved line that contains the following points: the point negative seven, negative two, the point negative five, three, the point negative three, three, the point zero, six point five, the point three, three, the point five, three, and the point nine, negative seven. The point negative three, three and the point nine, negative seven are connected by a solid line segment. There is a dashed segment from negative three, three to negative three, negative seven. There is another dashed segment from negative three, negative seven to nine, negative seven.

hints.content:
According to the graph, $f(\blue{-3})=\pink{3}$ and $f(\blue{9})=\pink{-7}$. Therefore, the average rate of change we are looking for is:

$\dfrac{\pink{-7}-\pink{3}}{\blue{9}-(\blue{-3})}=\dfrac{-10}{9+3}=-\dfrac{5}{6}$.
